project.name: cavet
project.description: A Go CLI security-triage tool for coding agents. It runs scanners (trivy, opengrep, gitleaks, checkov) inside an offline container engine and records every finding and decision in an append-only audit log.
project.context: This finding comes from a scan of the cavet repository itself.

finding.description:
To ensure reproducible builds, pin Dockerfile `FROM` commands to a specific hash. You can find the hash by running `docker pull debian` and then specify it with `debian:bookworm-slim@sha256:<hash goes here>`
verdict: dismissed (high confidence, by operator): floating the debian:bookworm-slim tag is deliberate and documented in the Dockerfile itself (lines 16-17): a digest-pinned base would freeze a stale apt snapshot, so the build runs apt-get -y upgrade to pull security updates instead; the golang builder stages remain digest-pinned (lines 41, 63)

criteria.false: Not actionable as a security issue in this project: either the security claim is wrong here (false positive, misread, safe as used) or the observation is genuinely valid but not a security concern (test fixture, non-shipped code, deliberate engineering choice).
